overview: Current law limits sales and transfers of U.S. military equipment to the Republic of Cyprus, an island nation in the eastern Mediterranean, but lets the President waive those limits one fiscal year at a time. This bill lets each such waiver last up to five fiscal years instead of one. It makes the same change in two existing laws: a 2019 Eastern Mediterranean security and energy law and the defense policy law for fiscal year 2020. As of October 30, 2025, a Senate committee had approved it and it was placed on the Senate's calendar, meaning it is eligible for a vote by the full Senate.
for: Supporters say Cyprus has become a closer security partner, and longer waivers would give both governments the predictability needed to plan defense purchases and cooperation instead of renewing approval every year.
against: Critics say the yearly waiver gives Congress and the executive branch a regular checkpoint on arms sales in a region with longstanding tensions, and stretching it to five years reduces that oversight.
